name: Token Grill
description:
Token Grill shows the usage limits of your Codex, Claude, Kiro, Antigravity, Copilot, OpenCode Go, Kimi Code, and Cursor accounts and your DeepSeek balance in the GNOME top bar. It monitors more than one account at the same time.

Token Grill needs its free companion service, tokengrill, from PyPI: run "pipx install tokengrill && ~/.local/bin/tokengrill setup". The service reads the sign-ins and contacts the hosts below; the extension only shows the results. The popup and Preferences can copy a fixed setup, update, or log command to the clipboard when you click its Copy button. Token Grill never reads the clipboard. When a sign-in has expired, "Sign In Again in a Terminal" in the popup opens the login command of that account's app in your terminal, only after you click it.

Token Grill reads the sign-ins that the app of each service, OpenCode, or Claude Code stored on this computer, and the DeepSeek API keys that you save in the GNOME keyring. Its HTTP client sends each credential only to its own service and connects only to these hosts:
* chatgpt.com (Codex)
* api.anthropic.com (Claude)
* The Amazon CodeWhisperer, Amazon Q, and AWS OIDC hosts of the region of your account (Kiro)
* cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com and oauth2.googleapis.com (Antigravity)
* api.github.com (Copilot)
* opencode.ai (OpenCode Go)
* api.deepseek.com (DeepSeek)
* api.kimi.com or api.kimi.ai (Kimi Code)
* api2.cursor.sh (Cursor)

For expired Claude Code sign-ins, the service runs the installed "claude auth status". Claude Code renews and saves its own credentials using its own network configuration, with nonessential traffic disabled. Token Grill then rereads the credentials.
